note: Phase 18 (BPMN e2e retirement, plan §5.3/§21.3) retargeted tests/e2e/lite-mandatory-reliability.spec.ts from the deleted bpmn-js Lite shell to the ARIS shell and found, by reading source and by driving the built app live, that the reliability subsystem this bundle was written against (src/App.tsx, src/sessions/*, src/workspace/dirtySave.ts, HistoryDialog.tsx, liveWorkspaceIndex.ts) is now entirely DEAD CODE: src/main.tsx renders only ArisApp.tsx, which has no dirty tracking (ProcessTabList is fed a hard-coded empty dirtyKeys set), no save affordance or Ctrl/Cmd+S handler, no reload-recovery journal, no external-edit-conflict dialog, no rename/move/delete UI, no revision-history dialog, no duplicate-process-ID repair, and no search/catalog screen. A second, independent tooling blocker (the shared reliability-fsa.ts fixture's fake directory handle throws DataCloneError inside ArisApp.tsx's rememberWorkspace, which predates the ARIS rewrite) additionally makes every directory-workspace path unreachable regardless of dirty-tracking. Of the original 13 tests / 11 requirement ids, only REL-06 (folder-picker cancellation) has both a real, reachable ARIS mechanism and a real assertion surface, and was retargeted. REL-01 through REL-05 and REL-07 through REL-11 are deliberately left unbound below (like UI-02/UI-03/UI-07 in mandatory-ui-accessibility-evidence.json): their browserTests entries intentionally still name the pre-retarget test titles, which no longer exist in the file, so the release-reporter gate fails honestly on each rather than silently passing or being rebound to an unrelated test. implementationAreas/implementationCommits/coverageNote on the unbound requirements below describe the deleted pre-ARIS architecture and are retained only as a historical record of what this bundle used to verify.

suite.resultNote: This file maps requirements to discoverable test titles. It deliberately does not manufacture or cache an execution result; CI or a retained Playwright report is authoritative for a particular commit.

fixtureSemantics.fileSystemAccess: The application uses its production DirectoryWorkspaceAdapter and document-session stack. The fixture supplies byte-backed picker handles because Playwright cannot operate Chromium's native folder chooser.
fixtureSemantics.opfs: The OPFS case uses each engine's real navigator.storage.getDirectory() on a loopback origin and the exact built dist/index.html. Playwright's WPE MiniBrowser disables its shipped StorageAPI, FileSystem, FileSystemWritableStream, and AccessHandle features by default and does not propagate startup feature settings to ordinary ephemeral contexts, so the WebKit path explicitly enables those supported features in an automatically cleaned-up temporary persistent context; no storage shim is installed.
fixtureSemantics.persistence: Fixture bytes, permissions, picker behavior, write failures, and write logs persist through localStorage so reload and cross-tab cases share backing state.
limitations: The fixture is not a native operating-system directory picker.
The suite is listed only for Chromium here; final Firefox and WebKit release evidence remains a separate gate.
REL-01 through REL-05 and REL-07 through REL-11 are unbound as of the ARIS retarget (see top-level note): the reliability subsystem they verified is dead code in the ARIS shell.
The 100 MiB aggregate history cap note below describes deleted pre-ARIS architecture and no longer applies.
